subject: Request: Temporary throughput-driven latency allowance + credit cap for EdgeNova migration
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@edgenova.com>
To: ava.chen@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Temporary latency allowance during migration window

Hi Ava,

Quick background — EdgeNova is planning a one-time large-scale ingest and index rebuild (migration) over a 6-week window starting 2027-01-10. Traffic simulations attached show 3-4x peak token throughput for short periods. Our infra team is nervous about p95 latency spikes during the window.

We have three asks:
- A temporary, timeboxed change to the latency SLO: allow p95 latency to increase from 120ms to 350ms for scheduled migration windows (expected ~4 hours, twice weekly) for 3 months.
- Cap on service credits tied to those scheduled windows (propose a max cumulative credit of $20k over the 3 months).
- Minor commercial concession: a one-time operational support discount of 10% on committed Dedicated capacity for the quarter.

We prefer to have this in an addendum rather than a full contract re-sign. Can you route to the right people and advise next steps? We need internal signoff by 2026-12-06 to meet procurement timelines.

Thanks,
Marta
VP of Platform Engineering
EdgeNova Systems

Attachments: edge_migration_traffic_report.csv (CSV, 48KB)
From: ava.chen@redwood.com
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Request: Temporary latency allowance during migration window

Ben/Grace — forwarding a time-sensitive request from EdgeNova (details above). Procurement needs an answer by 12/06. High level asks: 1) temporary SLO tolerance for scheduled windows (p95 120ms -> 350ms), 2) cap service credits, 3) 10% one-off discount on Dedicated commit for a quarter.

Initial thoughts: Ben, commercial impact and whether Deal Desk can accept a credit cap tied to scheduled windows.
Grace, can your team confirm whether we can set enforcement to exclude scheduled maintenance/migration windows from rolling SLO calculation, and whether there are safe guardrails (rate limits, preferential routing) we can require EdgeNova to follow?

I recommend we do a 3-week pilot clause and a strict monitoring/reporting cadence. If we need exec signoff we should prepare a short memo. Can someone pull estimated $ impact and put together proposed language for an addendum?

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

--- Forwarded attachment: proposed_contract_redline.pdf (PDF, 120KB)
From: grace.oconnor@redwood.com
To: ava.chen@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Temporary latency allowance during migration window

Ava/Ben — technical take and constraints:

1) Feasibility: We can implement a timeboxed exception where traffic during pre-defined migration windows is excluded from the rolling SLO calculation, but this must be explicit in the contract with exact UTC windows and a maximum of 8 events per month. We can also tag calls with a migration header so metrics pipeline excludes those spans.

2) Risks: allowing p95 to 350ms will increase tail behavior and could backpressure multi-tenant GPU pools. We’ll require EdgeNova to run a staged ramp (50% -> 100%) for the first two windows and share realtime telemetry. If their traffic exceeds the modelled ingress by >20% we need an automatic fallback (route to dedicated reserve capacity) — that costs extra but protects the rest of the fleet.

3) Controls: require:
- scheduled windows documented 7 days in advance,
- a max of 4 hours per event, 2 events per week (as Marta asked),
- telemetry sharing (Grafana read-only link) and weekly post-window readouts

4) Credits: I’m neutral on the cap; operationally we can tie a reduced credit formula to the scheduled windows (e.g., 50% of normal credit rate during excluded windows) but cap must be approved by finance.

I’ll draft the tech clause for the addendum and the fallback routing statement.

- Grace O'Connor
Director, Production Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
To: ava.chen@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Temporary latency allowance during migration window — Exec signoff

Team — after reviewing the ask and Grace’s mitigations, I approve a conditional executive signoff with these firm constraints:

1) Timebox: 3-month maximum (2027-01-10 through 2027-04-10).
2) Windows: up to 2 scheduled windows/week, max 4 hours each; windows must be submitted 7 days prior.
3) SLO Adjustment: p95 allowed up to 350ms only during the approved windows; all other times standard SLOs remain unchanged.
4) Credits: cap service credits tied to those windows at $20,000 cumulative over the 3 months (EdgeNova must accept this cap in the addendum).
5) Support/Commercial: approve the one-time 10% discount on Dedicated capacity for the single quarter, conditional on a 6-month minimum commit.
6) Fallback: if EdgeNova exceeds modelled traffic by >20% in any window we invoke automatic routing to a reserve pool; costs for reserve usage billed per standard rates and not covered by the credit cap.

Please prepare the addendum language and an internal memo summarizing financial exposure (Ben/Laurel — looking at you) and send to legal/deal-desk. I want a sign-off package ready for the 12/03 leadership call if we can.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
